title: Does clipping, per-channel scaling or quantisation-aware training move the 3-bit cliff of an MLP lane on real digits?
lede: MSE-optimal weight clipping lifts the 3-bit-weight digits MLP from 81% to 91% test accuracy at the same MAC-lane hardware and integer-exact; per-channel scales and QAT help at 4 bits (95.7% at W4A4, within 1.1 points of float) but QAT fails at 2 bits.
summary: Follow-up to chip-digits, whose max-scaled post-training quantisation collapsed at 3-bit weights (81% at W3A4 against 96.8% float). On the same 64-16-10 MLP and five scikit-learn digits splits, four quantisers are compared for W = 2–4, A = 3–5: the baseline max scale; a per-tensor scale chosen to minimise weight MSE (clipping); per-output-channel max scales; and quantisation-aware training (300 full-batch epochs, straight-through estimator). The two per-tensor methods are integer-exact in the same lane specification, so the lane gate counts of chip-digits apply unchanged. At W3A4 the accuracy is 80.7% (baseline), 90.8% (clip), 91.5% (per-channel, float rescale, not an integer lane) and 90.9% (QAT); at W4A4 94.8%, 94.4%, 95.7% and 95.7%; at W2 only clipping gets above 60% and QAT fine-tuning is worse than the baseline at A=3 (28.5% against 32.8%). Limitations: one small network and dataset, five splits (minimum accuracies are in results.txt, spreads of several points at W≤3), QAT hyperparameters untuned, per-channel rescale hardware not built or costed, generic gates not area. All inputs are measured on the dataset; none is assumed.
